mutations.change_summary: Proposed: change the contract of saveStateBeforeParse/restoreStateBeforeParse so repeated parse() calls are allowed even when storeOptionsAsProperties is true (currently throws), and the saved state includes the option-description registry snapshot.

before.behavior: restoreStateBeforeParse() throws when this._storeOptionsAsProperties is true (command.js:1158-1161); otherwise resets _name, _scriptPath, rawArgs, _optionValues, _optionValueSources, args, processedArgs from _savedState (shallow clones). saveStateBeforeParse() snapshots _name, _optionValues, _optionValueSources only (1141-1150). _prepareForParse (1127-1133) calls save on first parse, restore on subsequent parses.

after.behavior: Restore no longer throws under storeOptionsAsProperties; state snapshot is extended (e.g. option registry / command registry); restore path must also clear any state mutated by parseOptions and _processArguments beyond the five fields.

ground_truth.gt_status: DRAFT — dual-evaluator calibration pending (protocol v1.1 §4.2), NOT frozen

impact_chain.evidence: 1141-1150; snapshot fields define what restore can reset
1158-1174; throw condition is the contract under test
1127-1133; save/restore dispatcher
repeated-parse semantics; _prepareForParse is invoked from parse
existing tests assert the throw for storeOptionsAsProperties re-parse
documented limitation for storeOptionsAsProperties + parse twice
public method signature; extension-point for subclasses

critical_edges: storeOptionsAsProperties throw → allowed (behavioral contract flip; consumers may depend on the error)
saved-state field set → restore completeness (new registry fields must be reset or stale across parses)
ground_truth.gt_note: Chain semantics: change → dependency (save/restore pair + parse) → behavior (repeat-parse allowed, registry reset) → contract (public method + error contract + typings).

mutations.change_summary: Proposed: configureHelp() gains a second optional parameter 'base' selecting whether the returned Help instance inherits from a user-supplied Help subclass or from the default Help; merging changes from Object.assign to explicit property copy that preserves getters.

before.behavior: configureHelp(configuration) stores configuration verbatim; getter returns it; createHelp() = Object.assign(new Help(), this.configureHelp()) (command.js:198-204, 215-220). Help customization happens via property assignment; getters in configuration are lost by Object.assign.

after.behavior: configureHelp(configuration, base) accepts a Help base class; createHelp() merges with property descriptors preserved; existing single-arg call sites keep working (backward-compatible default).

ground_truth.gt_status: DRAFT — dual-evaluator calibration pending (protocol v1.1 §4.2), NOT frozen

impact_chain.evidence: 215-220; signature change ripples to call sites
198-204; merge strategy is the customization seam
Help instances produced by createHelp; property-based customization surface
all help rendering flows through createHelp
documents configureHelp() customization
configureHelp tests assert merge behavior
public API typing; new parameter must be typed

critical_edges: configureHelp → createHelp merge (Object.assign vs descriptor-preserving copy; getters currently dropped — behavior change)
createHelp → helpInformation → outputHelp (every help render path)
Help subclass base → visible*/stringify overrides (docs/help-in-depth customization contract)
ground_truth.gt_note: Chain semantics: change → dependency (createHelp merge + Help class) → behavior (render pipeline output) → contract (public configureHelp signature + typings).

mutations.change_summary: Proposed: extract the executable-file resolution (findFile + extension probing + realpath) from _executeSubCommand into a standalone module lib/resolveExecutable.js, and switch default extension probing order to prefer .js over .ts/.tsx (currently all probed with no order guarantee).

before.behavior: _executeSubCommand (command.js:1202-1346) does inline findFile with sourceExt ['.js','.ts','.tsx','.mjs','.cjs'], realpath resolution, mandatory/conflicting option checks before spawn, node-launch for source files, inspector port increments. Dispatch call at command.js:1365.

after.behavior: File resolution moved to new lib/resolveExecutable.js with deterministic extension order; _executeSubCommand imports it; resolution errors surface with same messages; no behavioral change to spawn/validation flow.

ground_truth.gt_status: DRAFT — dual-evaluator calibration pending (protocol v1.1 §4.2), NOT frozen

impact_chain.evidence: 1202-1346; resolution logic removed/replaced by module call
new file; zero-dep policy means it must be hand-rolled in-tree (GT-C02)
1363-1369; passes operands+unknown into execute path
1224-1226; must stay in parent regardless of module extraction
extension probing and error-message assertions
documented file-naming convention <parent>-<subcommand> (Readme 700-723)
new lib file is internal (not exported); zero-dep and exports-map check (GT-C18)

critical_edges: resolution order change → existing projects with both .ts and .js executables pick different file (silent behavior change)
module extraction → zero-dep policy and in-tree utility rule (GT-C02)
error messages/surface → tests asserting 'Cannot find executable' text
ground_truth.gt_note: Chain semantics: change → dependency (dispatch → execute → resolve module) → behavior (which file wins probing order) → contract (executable naming convention, docs).

mutations.change_summary: Proposed: move the excess-arguments check from _processArguments (post-parse) into parseOptions' operand loop (pre-dispatch), so excess detection happens before subcommand dispatch and subcommands can no longer observe excess parent operands.

before.behavior: _excessArguments (command.js:2146-2154) is called from _processArguments (1418) after parsing; compares received args to registeredArguments.length; throws commander.excessArguments unless _allowExcessArguments. Subcommand dispatch happens later (1352-1371).

after.behavior: Excess check fires inside parseOptions operand collection; parent operands in excess are rejected before any subcommand gets them; error code/message unchanged; allowExcessArguments escape still honored.

ground_truth.gt_status: DRAFT — dual-evaluator calibration pending (protocol v1.1 §4.2), NOT frozen

impact_chain.evidence: operand loop; insertion point changes when excess is detected
2146-2154; call site moves; message/args computation may need operand-count context
1418; check removed from here
1352-1371; subcommand no longer receives excess parent operands (cross-level argument passing, GT-C06/C09 cluster)
excess-argument error timing assertions
documents allowExcessArguments and default strictness (GT-C04)

critical_edges: check timing vs subcommand dispatch (behavior change: excess parent operands rejected pre-dispatch — GT-C06/C09 recursion semantics)
allowExcessArguments escape (must still work from parseOptions path)
error message 'too many arguments ... got N' (message parity across moved call site)
ground_truth.gt_note: Chain semantics: change → dependency (parseOptions operand loop + dispatch) → behavior (excess detection timing) → contract (error code commander.excessArguments + documented strictness).

mutations.change_summary: Proposed: add a new stable error code commander.invalidArgumentValue emitted when parseArg throws a non-CommanderError, while preserving commander.invalidArgument for InvalidArgumentError instances; update exitOverride docs and tests accordingly.

before.behavior: InvalidArgumentError carries code 'commander.invalidArgument' (lib/error.js:13-19). _callParseArg (command.js:599-604) wraps parseArg exceptions: if err.code === 'commander.invalidArgument' it prepends invalidArgumentMessage, otherwise rethrows the original error. exitOverride tests assert exact (code,message) pairs as 'intended to be stable' (tests/command.exitOverride.test.js:5-13,51-435).

after.behavior: Non-CommanderError throws from parseArg are caught and re-emitted as CommanderError with code commander.invalidArgumentValue; InvalidArgumentError path unchanged; both codes documented in exitOverride docs.

ground_truth.gt_status: DRAFT — dual-evaluator calibration pending (protocol v1.1 §4.2), NOT frozen

impact_chain.evidence: 590-610; catch/re-wrap logic is the change site

asserts exact stable code pairs; new code must be added there

code field semantics; new code value is a public contract

critical_edges: error-code stability contract (GT-C29): consumers match on code, not message; adding a code is additive, but re-classifying an existing failure path changes what consumers see
exitOverride test suite exact-pair assertions (intended-to-be-stable list must be extended)
ground_truth.gt_note: Chain semantics: change → dependency (parseArg failures via value pipeline) → behavior (which error class/code a failure yields) → contract (stable code list, docs, typings).

mutations.change_summary: Proposed: change the missingMandatoryOptionValue error code from commander.missingMandatoryOptionValue to commander.missingMandatoryOptionValue (message unchanged) is NOT the proposal — the proposal is: message gains the option flags string, and the code stays stable; only the message composition changes.

before.behavior: missingMandatoryOptionValue(option) (command.js:2058-2060) calls this.error(message, { code: 'commander.missingMandatoryOptionValue' }); invoked from _checkForMissingMandatoryOptions (1683) during dispatch precedence. Message currently 'error: required option ... not specified'.

after.behavior: Message includes option flags (e.g. '-r, --required <value>') and hint of the missing-value condition; code unchanged; exitOverride tests updated only for message text.

ground_truth.gt_status: DRAFT — dual-evaluator calibration pending (protocol v1.1 §4.2), NOT frozen

1683; caller passes the offending option
